title: Eden: It's an Endless World!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: After a virus has killed much of humanity, a world government called Propater rules by force (to verify). Elijah Ballard, son of a former Propater opponent, grows up amid cartels, wars and terrorism in South America and beyond, accompanied by a combat AI, as the story asks what humanity is and whether it deserves to survive (to verify).
life_message: It suggests meaning has to be made in a violent world through loyalty, survival and choosing one's own path (to verify).

content.note: Teen Elijah becomes a hardened killer while fleeing Propater; Kenji kills soldiers and non-combatants without visible remorse; a reviewer says the combat overshadows the characters (Wikipedia); ANN calls it 'a military action thriller' with praised action scenes. Gore level beyond this not confirmed (AniList Gore 88%).

delivery.evidence: ANN review of vols. 1-2: beats the reader over the head with pedantic philosophical and (anti-)religious statements; dialogue called mechanical
delivery.note: Characters voice philosophical and religious arguments directly, which the cited reviewer finds heavy-handed.

winners_losers: Survivors who hold to personal loyalty against Propater get the sympathy; neither the regime nor the cartels win cleanly. A bleak existentialist worldview gets the most space (to verify).
